# Anymake

> Agentic build system. Takes any software idea — SaaS, CLI, library, API, internal tool, static site, or hobby project — from raw concept to a finished, shipped result through a six-phase, artifact-driven methodology that adapts to what you're building, with a built-in multi-agent implementation engine.

## What Anymake is

Anymake is an AI skill for [OpenCode.ai](https://opencode.ai) that guides product development through six disciplined phases — Foundation, Discovery, Planning, Solutioning, Implementation, and Launch — producing a concrete artifact at every step, requiring user approval at every phase gate, and autonomously building the product in Phase 4 with a five-stage agent system.

Anymake is markdown-as-source-of-truth (ADR-008): no build step, no runtime, no service. The instruction files *are* the system, which is why they have a regression suite (`npm run verify`) that runs in CI on every push.

**Install:**
```json
{ "plugin": ["anymake@git+https://github.com/R3dy/Anymake.git"] }
```
Add to `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`, then restart OpenCode.

**Trigger:** Say "Start a new project" or "Continue [project name]".

## Core concepts

- **Phases** — Six sequential phases, each gated on user approval before advancing
- **Artifacts** — Every phase produces a document. Documents are truth; conversation memory is not
- **One step per session** — Prevents scope creep; every session ends with a clear artifact and named next action
- **PHASE_STATE.md** — The system's bookmark; records current phase, step, last artifact, and next action
- **PARKING_LOT.md** — Scope requests that arrive mid-phase; logged, never acted on without a new gate
- **BOARD.md** — Live agile board updated after every Phase 4 agent action; a rendered projection of `board-state.json`, not a separate source
- **board-state.json** — The structured taskboard spine (`.anymake/board-state.json`, schema in `TEMPLATES/board-state.schema.json`). The orchestrator is its sole writer; agents append events; the kanban dashboard reads it directly
- **Worktree isolation** — Each story builds in its own git worktree, so concurrent stories never collide on a shared checkout
- **Project types** — `saas`, `hobby`, `cli`, `library`, `api-service`, `internal-tool`, `static-site`, `agentic-harness`. The type is chosen at project creation, stored in `PHASE_STATE.md`, and drives the phase map, build order, and gate criteria (`PROJECT_TYPES/<id>/manifest.md`)

## The six phases

- Phase 0 – Foundation: Define elevator pitch, scope, revenue model, success metrics → `PROJECT.md`
- Phase 1 – Discovery: Market research, competitor analysis, user personas, risk register → `docs/01-discovery.md`
- Phase 2 – Planning: PRD, UX design system + prototype, architecture decisions (ADRs), monetization plan
- Phase 3 – Solutioning: Epics, user stories with acceptance criteria, ordered backlog, dependency graph
- Phase 4 – Implementation: Scaffold → Auth → Agentic build loop → Security review → Staging deploy
- Phase 5 – Launch: Live deployment, metrics dashboard, growth loop

## Phase 4 agent system

Five-stage autonomous build loop in `AGENTS/`. **Stories run in parallel; stages within a story do not** — each story's Planner → Worker → Validator → Experience Runner pipeline is strictly sequential, while different non-conflicting stories are dispatched concurrently up to `concurrency.max` (default 3). Two stories conflict iff their `touches_files` sets intersect or one depends on the other. `concurrency.max: 1` reproduces sequential behavior.

- **Orchestrator** — Team lead. Reconciles `board-state.json`, renders BOARD.md from it, dispatches ready non-conflicting stories concurrently, watches for stalls, applies the retry matrix per story, enforces PR policy, escalates only when blocked. Never writes code or authors brief content
- **Planner** — Translates one approved story (plus ADRs, the intent layer, and `CONVENTIONS.md`) into a self-contained task brief including a literal §3a Experience Script and `touches_files`. Never writes code
- **Worker** — Receives the approved brief, implements in the layer order from that brief (manifest-derived per project type; SaaS default Schema → Migration → API → Component → Page → Integration → Test), commits each layer, opens a PR — all inside the story's own git worktree
- **Validator** — Checks every acceptance criterion, runs the security checklist, and runs the intent-consistency check against every decision/invariant listed in §6a *plus any other the change plausibly touches*. Returns PASS / FAIL / ESCALATE
- **Experience Runner** — Launches the real app on the story's branch and drives it against the §3a script, comparing observed to expected step by step. A Validator PASS alone never clears a story. Observes and diagnoses; never edits code
- **Cartographer** (post-launch, read-only) — maps the as-built code to intent and maintains the engineering-intent layer (`docs/SYSTEM_MAP.md`, `DECISIONS.md`, `INVARIANTS.md`) that `anymake-agile` checks future changes against
- **Solution Architect** (post-launch) — reviews the full project and writes the Development Plan for one tracked issue; never touches code
- **Plan Reviewer** (post-launch) — fresh-context adversarial review of each Development Plan; approves, demands changes, or escalates before anything is built
- **Product Owner Proxy** — autonomous-mode gate evaluator; applies strict per-gate criteria and returns APPROVED / NEEDS CHANGES / ESCALATE TO USER. Security failures always escalate to the real user
- **Arbiter** — the shared rulebook every agent defers to (not spawned, read): retry matrix, PR review rules (PRs 1–3; any inbound third-party callback — webhook, OAuth redirect, payment return URL, queue subscriber; any ADR-touching story), escalation phrase lexicon, failure classification, intent conflict policy, agile plan review policy, model tier policy, the INV-018 dispatch scope, the definition of "the security baseline", and the project-type / "Never Building" scope guardrails

**All dispatch goes through the `anymake-dispatch` skill** (INV-018) — never a raw Agent/Task call. The skill adds pre-dispatch prompt assembly (WRITE THE FILE FIRST), a mandatory post-dispatch deliverable check, canonical retry context, and a dispatch log line. It is also the only place the host runtime is named, so porting to another harness is a one-section change. Read-only research delegation is the single documented exemption.

## Skill suite

Anymake is a plugin that ships a **hub** skill (`anymake`) plus focused **companion** skills the hub delegates to at the right phase/step (each also usable standalone):

- **anymake-build-loop** — the five-stage Orchestrator → Planner → Worker → Validator → Experience Runner build engine (Phase 4.3)
- **anymake-dispatch** — the single chokepoint for all sub-agent dispatch (INV-018); the host-portability seam
- **anymake-experience-setup** — builds the testing harness: Experience Scripts across a backlog, coverage audit, `docs/environment.md` (Phase 3.2b)
- **anymake-experience-check** — uses the testing harness on demand: drive a story, PR, or staging/production URL outside the build loop
- **anymake-design-system** — design system + Prototype Sprint + prototype-gate audit (Phase 2.2b)
- **anymake-security-review** — per-PR, full, and pre-launch security checklists (Phase 4.5, pre-launch)
- **anymake-deploy** — staging + production deployment, env/secrets, monitoring, rollback (Phase 4 staging, Phase 5.2)
- **anymake-brownfield** — reverse-engineer Phase 0–3 artifacts from an existing codebase (in place of Phase 0)
- **anymake-iterate** — post-launch loop: triage, metrics→epics, releases (Phase 5.6 onward)
- **anymake-agile** — the single post-launch pipeline for changing a built product (bug reports and add/change/remove requests): confirmed intake → labeled GitHub issue → Solution Architect development plan checked against the engineering-intent layer → independent Plan Reviewer approval → traceable build via anymake-build-loop → reporter verification
- **anymake-new-type** — scaffold a new project-type profile

See `skills/README.md` for the full map.

## Autonomous mode (yolo)

Activated by adding `--yolo` to any project trigger. Dispatches a **Product Owner Proxy** sub-agent (`AGENTS/product-owner-proxy.md`) at each phase gate instead of waiting for human approval. The proxy applies strict per-gate criteria and returns APPROVED, specific required changes, or ESCALATE TO USER. Autonomous mode is recorded in `PHASE_STATE.md` as `autonomous_mode: true`.

What autonomous mode cannot do, by design:

- **Security failures always escalate to the real user**, in every mode. Absolute, no exception
- **A gate that can't check something must say so.** Approving while waiving a judgment requires a `LIMITATION:` line in the verdict naming what specifically went unverified, logged permanently to BOARD.md's Gate Decisions table. An `APPROVED` that hides an unchecked judgment is malformed
- **It cannot reopen a scope boundary.** A story matching `PROJECT.md`'s "Never Building" list fails the gate; only a Phase 0 scope amendment the real user approves can change that
- **It cannot change `project_type`** — that's a product decision. Where a project's own words suggest the type is wrong (a `hobby` project with pricing and paying customers), the system surfaces a one-line advisory and continues; it never switches or blocks
- **It cannot substitute code for evidence.** A Human-Only criterion is satisfied by an Experience Runner PASS, never by confirming the relevant code exists

## Verification

This repo has no build step and no runtime, so the instruction files are checked against each
other instead:

```bash
npm run verify            # the regression harness — 24 check groups, zero dependencies
npm run validate-board    # validate a board-state.json against the schema
```

`.github/workflows/verify.yml` runs it on every push and PR. Among other things it executes every
dispatch verification command against the real template it targets (a check that can never match
its own template fails every valid deliverable), enforces the dispatch chokepoint, checks that
root `AGENTS.md` doesn't contradict the detailed specs it summarizes, confirms the dashboard has a
column for every schema story status, and dry-runs the build loop against fixture deliverables.

The repo convention: **every instruction fix ships with the assertion that would have caught it.**

## Precedence

`AGENTS.md` is a summary. Wherever it and a detailed `AGENTS/*.md` file disagree, **the detailed
file wins**; `AGENTS/arbiter.md` is authoritative on all shared policy. In agent-instruction files,
"you" addresses the agent being instructed — the human is always "the user" or "the real user."
